Ishan Rao: Hi folks, first day. Trying to run the example in the \"playpen\" namespace but `kubectl get ns playpen` says not found. I used Okta SSO to populate kubeconfig. Any quick checks?

Nina Ortiz: welcome Ishan! :wave: run `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n playpen`. Also `kubectl config view --minify` to see which user is attached.

Ishan Rao: current-context = redwood-dev, `kubectl config view --minify` -> user is ishan@okta, `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n playpen` -> no. Tried `kubectl --as=system:serviceaccount:playpen:dev-sa get pods` -> forbidden (cannot impersonate).

Nina Ortiz: sounds like RBAC. For new hires we either grant a temporary RoleBinding or give an ephemeral service-account token. Which do you want to unblock you quickly?

Ishan Rao: RoleBinding is fine for now, want to finish the tutorial.

Nina Ortiz: @eng-infra-bot please create an infra ticket to bind `ishan@okta` to `edit` in `playpen`.

eng-infra-bot: Created INFRA-5101: \"Playpen access - Ishan Rao\". Assignee: @platform-oncall. ETA 1h.

platform-oncall: Hi Ishan 44b applied a 24h RoleBinding for `ishan@okta` in `playpen`. Verify with:

`kubectl auth can-i list pods -n playpen`
`kubectl get pods -n playpen`

Ishan Rao: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n playpen` -> yes now. `kubectl get pods -n playpen` -> shows demo pods. Thanks everyone! :tada:

Nina Ortiz: For later, SA token flow (k8s >=1.24):

`kubectl create token dev-sa -n playpen`
`kubectl config set-credentials play-sa --token=\"$(kubectl create token dev-sa -n playpen)\"`
`kubectl config set-context play-sa-ctx --cluster=gke-redwood-dev --user=play-sa --namespace=playpen`

That avoids giving direct user RBAC for automation.

onboarding-bot: \u2705 K8s access granted, INFRA-5101 linked to ONBOARD-271. Checklist updated.
